headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 18 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: Four days to go to Granada, and today’s stage is a decisive one with a 32.1 km individual time trial from El Puerto de Santa Maria to Jerez de la Frontera. Powerhouses will battle for the stage win and GC contenders will test their strength ahead of the two final mountain showdowns. Mathias Sunekær Norsgaard will be the first rider off the ramp, at 14:07; Enric Mas will the last, at 16:55. The Spaniard will finish his effort at around 17:30.

headline: From Sunekær Norsgaard to Mas
subtext: The 149 riders who finished yesterday’s stage will start in reverse order of the overall standings, from last to first. Matias Sunekær Norsgaard (Lidl-Trek) will go first, at 14:07. He will be followed a minute later by Paul Double (Jayco AlUla), then Louis Rouland (Cofidis), Domen Novak (UAE Emirates XRG), Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step)… The starts will continue at one-minute intervals until Raul Garcia Pierna (Movistar) sets off at 16:15. Then, the top 20 riders in GC will go every two minutes, finishing with the current overall podium: Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) at 16:51, Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) at 16:53, and eventually Enric Mas (Movistar) at 16:55.

headline: La Roja
subtext: Enric Mas (Movistar) tackles three decisive stages with a lead of 2’06’’ on Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) and 2’10’’ on Primoz Roglic.

headline: Green jersey
subtext: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) keeps racking points, up to 295 ahead of the final four stages. With a fifth stage win in La Rabida, his teammate Matthew Brennan now has 239 points. Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) is still third with 171 points. Mathematically, Romele is the only rider who can still challenge Van Aert and Brennan. Van Aert needs to score 7 more points than the Italian youngster to rule him out for good. A rider can grab a maximum of 150 points on the final four stages, including 20 today.

headline: Polka dot jersey
subtext: Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) still leads the mountains standings with 69 points, a tally that gives him a significant margin on Wout van Aert (40 points). Enric Mas (Movistar) follows with 24 points. There are 53 points up for grabs this week, but they’re all packed in stages 19 (20 points) and 20 (33 points).

headline: White jersey
subtext: Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) is still 30’’ ahead of Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious) while Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) trails by 10’41’’.

headline: Team standings
subtext: Decathlon CMA CGM are strong leaders of the overall team standings with a gap of 57’32’’ to XDS Astana and 1h11’15’’ to Bahrain Victorious.

headline: Combativity award
subtext: Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ Untied) will race with a distinctive bib again as he was named the most combative rider yesterday.

headline: Welcome to Cadiz and El Puerto de Santa Maria
subtext: After Almeria, Granada, Jean, Cordoba, Huelva and Seville, La Vuelta 26 completes its Andalusian tour with a stage entirely set in the province of Cadiz. The race will have visited the autonomous community’s eight provinces once it settles in Malaga with stage 19, before returning to Granada for the final two days. El Puerto de Santa Maria makes its debut as a La Vuelta stage town*. It was the setting of Vuelta a Andalucia stages a handful of times in the 1960s and 1970s. *The full list of new stage towns in this edition: Monaco (stage 1), Manosque (2), Font-Romeu (stage 3), Falset (5), Roquetes (5), Vall d’Alba (7), Puçol (8), Xeraco (8), La Vila Joiosa (9), Alcaraz (10), Elche de la Sierra (10), Vera (12), Almuñécar (13), Palma del Rio (15), Cortegana (16), La Rábida (16), Dos Hermanas (17), El Puerto de Santa María (18), La Calahorra (20), and Collado del Aguacil (20).

headline: Memories from Jerez de la Frontera: O’Connor, Pino, Contador…
subtext: Jerez de la Frontera is a classic venue that first hosted a La Vuelta stage in 1950 and most recently saw the peloton set off to Yunquera on stage 6 of the 2024 edition, the day after Pavel Bittner’s victory in Seville. Primoz Roglic was wearing La Roja at the start. Ben O’Connor achieved a spectacular breakaway to win the stage and take the overall leader’s jersey. He kept it for 13 days before Roglic took it back two days before his fourth overall victory. Today’s time trial echoes the final stage of the 1986 edition of La Vuelta, a 20-km effort in Jerez de la Frontera to conclude the race. Alvaro Pino led the overall standings with a gap of 33 seconds to Robert Millar at the start of the day, and the Spaniard won the final stage ahead of Laurent Fignon and Sean Kelly to seal his overall victory. Jerez de la Frontera was also the setting of the Gran Salida of La Vuelta in 1979, 1984, 1992 and 2014. The 2014 edition is the last to have crowned a Spanish overall winner of La Vuelta (Alberto Contador). Three riders who participated in La Vuelta 14 are back in Jerez de la Frontera today: Pello Bilbao, Mikel Landa, and Larry Warbasse. Both Bilbao and Warbasse ware making their debut in Grand Tours.

headline: Stage 18 is ON!
subtext: Matias Sunekær Norsgaard (Lidl-Trek) rolls down the ramp. He will be followed in a minute by Paul Double (Jayco AlUla), then Louis Rouland (Cofidis), Domen Novak (UAE Emirates XRG), Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step)…

headline: Hayter is the first reigning ITT champion to start
subtext: 14:11 - Ethan Hayter, Great Britain 14:47 - Yevgeniy Fedorov, Asia + Kazakhstan 14:48 - Pablo Castrillo, Spain 15:24 - Finn Fisher-Black, New Zealand 16:51 - Primoz Roglic, Slovenia Orluis Aular was Venezuela’s ITT champion for the Gran Salida in Monaco, but the 2026 edition of the Venezuelan national championships was held early September and Francisco Joel Peñuela won the men elite ITT.

headline: Early contenders
subtext: After Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step), who saw Tadej Pogacar snatch the win from him with the nearest margin in Monaco, Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) will start at 14:19. The young Scot was 4th in Monaco, behind Pogacar, Hayter and Tarling. He said yesterday he aims for a top 3 result... "But in the back of my mind I just want to win the stage", he added. "It would be amazing. It’s a big dream. If I had to design a course, I think it’s perfect for me. I think the first one was a little bit too punchy and too short for me, but this one being longer, 35 minutes, it’s perfect for me really.”

headline: First benchmarks
subtext: Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) passes the first intermediate checkpoint (km 11.7) with a time of 12'41''. That's 40 seconds faster than Mathias Sunekær Norsgaard (Lidl-Trek). Domen Novak (UAE Emirates XRG) trails by 42 seconds, and Louis Rouland (Cofidis) by 55''.

headline: Thornley starts stronger than Hayter
subtext: At km 11.7, the Scotsman is 19 seconds faster than the Londoner.

headline: Chamberlain in the mix?
subtext: The young Aussie takes the third best time at the first intermediate checkpoint, 27'' behind Thornley. He was 7th in the opening ITT in Monaco.

headline: An early battle between Thornley and Hayter
subtext: Callum Thornley was leading by 19'' at the first intermediate checkpoint (km 11.7), and he pushes his advantage to 23'' as he passes km 22.1 with a time of 23'47''.

headline: Sunekær Norsgaard is the first rider to finish
subtext: His time to cover the day's 32.1 km: 37'30''.

headline: Hayter has finished his effort
subtext: His time at the line: 35'54''. That's 1'36'' ahead of Mathias Sunekær Norsgaard. But will it be enough to resist Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe)?

headline: Thornley stronger than Hayter
subtext: Fourth in the opening time trial, Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) believes he can do better with today's longer effort. He takes the best time at the finish: 35'25''. That's 29'' faster than Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step).

headline: Chamberlain sets the 3rd best time at the finish
subtext: 1. Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) 2. Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step), +29'' 3. Oscar Chamberlain (Decathlon CMA CGM), +51''

headline: Oliveira to threaten Thornley's time?
subtext: Ivo Oliveira trailed by 7'' at the first checkpoint (km 11.7) and 11'' at the second (km 22.1).

headline: Azparren started strong
subtext: The runner-up in the ITT of the 2026 Spain national championships sets the second best time after 11.7 km: 12'27'' (+6'').

headline: 2nd best time for Oliveira
subtext: 1. Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) 2. Ivo Oliveira (UAE Emirates XRG), +27'' 3. Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step), +29''

headline: Almeida starts stronger than Thornley
subtext: The Portuguese takes the best time at km 11.7: 12'19'', almost 3 seconds faster than Thornley.

headline: Thornley: "You can do a lot of damage in the second part of the course"
subtext: Callum Thornley's first reaction after setting the best time: "I took a look at the simulation and I think it was 35:35, so I've been 10 seconds faster! I'm really happy with that time, specially beating Ethan [Hayter] by that margin. I'm really happy. I think the team managed the fatigue quite well at this race. At the start of the race this TT wasn't a go, because just making it to the stage 18 was the most important thing in my first Grand Tour. But yeah, to beat Ethan by that and hopefully a good result in the end, I will be happy with that. I think you can do a lot of damage in the second part of the course. We all know that the corners here are super slippery, specially in the villages and the towns. I'll probably phone [Primoz Roglic] and give him some advice, but he will do well."

headline: A tight battle between Almeida and Thornley
subtext: The Portuguese star was 2.81 seconds ahead of the young Scostman after 11.7 km, but he trails by 0.27 second at km 22.1.

headline: 4th best time for Azparren at the finish
subtext: The Spaniard is 30 seconds behind Thornley, 1 second behind Hayter.

headline: Specialists at the start
subtext: Bruno Armirail (Visma-Lease a Bike) just started his effort. Stefan Küng (Tudor) sets off two minutes after the Frenchman.

headline: The top 5 after 50 riders completed the stage
subtext: 1. Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) 2. Ivo Oliveira (UAE Emirates XRG) +27'' 3. Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) +29'' 4. Xabier Azparren (Pinarello-Q36.5) +30" 5. Georg Steinhauser (EF Education-EasyPost) +45"

headline: Almeida finishes behind Thornley
subtext: The Portuguese trails by 6'' at the finish.

headline: Romele won't score points today
subtext: So if Wout van Aert finishes in the stage's top 9, the Italian will be more than 130 points behind, and the green jersey will be all but secured for Visma-Lease a Bike.

headline: Küng challenges Thornley's benchmark
subtext: After 11.7 km, the Swiss specialist is 1 second behind Almeida and 1 second ahead of Thornley. Armirail is 11 seconds behind Küng (7th time).

headline: Küng, one of two La Vuelta ITT winners at the start
subtext: Stefan Küng (Tudor) won the final ITT of La Vuelta 24, in Madrid. Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) has won four in 2019, 2020, and 2021 (x2).

headline: Küng pushes the pace, Van Aert is behind
subtext: At the first checkpoint (km 22.1), Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) has the 4th best time, 6 seconds behind Joao Almeida (UAE Emirates XRG) and 3 seconds behind Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe). At the second checkpoint, Stefan Küng (Tudor) is 11 seconds faster than Thornley.

headline: Wout van Aert (Visma | Lease a Bike)
Küng just ahead of Thornley
subtext: 1. Stefan Küng (Tudor), 35'22'' 2. Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), +3'' 3. Joao Almeida (UAE Emirates XRG), +9'' 4. Finn Fisher-Black (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), +21'' 5. Bruno Armirail (Visma-Lease a Bike), +26''

headline: Can Van Aert beat Küng?
subtext: Wout van Aert sets the second best time at km 22.1, 7.16 seconds behind Küng and 3.73 seconds ahead of Thornley. At the finish, the Swiss rouleur was just 2.27 seconds ahead of the Scotsman.

headline: It's time for the top 15 riders in GC
subtext: Mario Aparicio (Burgos Burpellet BH) just began his effort. He will be folowed by Juan Felipe Rodriguez (EF Education-EasyPost).

headline: 4th best time for Van Aert
subtext: The Belgian star faded in the final part of the stage. He crosses the line with a gap of 20 seconds.

headline: Wout van Aert (Visma I Lease a Bike)
Kuss just started
subtext: It's time for the top 10 riders overall to tackle today's 32.1 km effort.

headline: Küng: "I hope it's enough to win"
subtext: Stefan Küng's reaction after setting the best time so far: "It's always hard a TT in the 3rd week of a Grand Tour. You just have to go as hard as you can and try to hang on. Honestly, some corners looked super slippery today, so I was not so confident in that, but I had power to push until the finish and I think it that's where I made the difference. I felt like I still had a little bit left towards the end, but it's always hard in the 3rd week of a Grand Tour. I gave it my all so I have be happy with today, I hope it's enough to win."

headline: Carapaz starts
subtext: The Ecuadorian star is 4th on GC, 2'14'' behind Roglic.

headline: Mas begins his effort
subtext: The GC battle is in full swing as the Spaniard aims to defend a lead of 2'06'' to Felix Gall and 2'10'' to Primoz Roglic.

headline: The GC contenders at the first intermediate
subtext: Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) is the fastest of them, with the 7th best time, 9 seconds behind Almeida. The Slovenian gains 14 seconds on Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos), 22 on Enric Mas (Movistar) and Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM), 23 on Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost)...

headline: Onley is faster than Omrzel
subtext: After 22.1 km, Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) has the 14th best time, 46'' behind Stefan Küng (Tudor) and 29'' ahead of Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious).

headline: 6th time for Roglic at the 2nd intermediate
subtext: The Slovenian is 14'' behind Küng.

headline: Mas 36 seconds behind Roglic after 22.1 km
subtext: The Spaniard is 21 seconds faster than Gall.

headline: 15th time for Onley: 36'33''
subtext: The British wearer of the white jersey was 27 seconds faster than Omrzel.

headline: 4th best time for Roglic (+19'')
subtext: How much time will he gain on his GC rivals?

headline: 25th time for Gall
subtext: The Austrian was 1'28'' slower than Roglic, who overtakes him in the overall standings.

headline: Enric Mas finishes with the 12th time
subtext: The Spaniard loses 33 seconds to Roglic. He was 55 seconds faster than Gall.

headline: Stefan Küng wins stage 18 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: The Swiss specialist takes his second win in La Vuelta after the final ITT of the 2024 edition. He covered the 32.1 km in 35’22’’82 (54.4km/h).

headline: Top 5
subtext: 1. Stefan Küng (Tudor), 35’22’’ 2. Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), +3’’ 3. Joao Almeida (UAE Emirates XRG), +9’’ 4. Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), +19’’ 5. Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike), +20’’

headline: Roglic is 1'37'' behind Mas overall
subtext: 1. Enric Mas (Movistar) 2. Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), +1’37’’ 3. Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM), +3’01’’ 4. Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost), +5’17’’ 5. Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos), +6’03’’
